target_customer: Freight carriers and logistics companies in Korea and the United States
problem: Long-haul trucking faces driver shortages and high costs; Mars Auto builds camera-based autonomous Class 8 trucks.
business_model: Autonomous freight service and trucking operations, with technology licensing ambitions

founders.name: Ilsu Park
founders.background_notes: Education from a May 2022 KoreaTechDesk article. A second KAIST computer science co-founder is described there without a name; yespress profiles name Gyuri Im, which was not confirmed by a company source, so not listed.

competitors.name: TuSimple
competitors.funding_then: About $95M raised in February 2019 at a reported $1B valuation

technical_complexity.rationale: Full-stack autonomous driving for Class 8 trucks on public roads with a camera-first approach and no HD maps is research-grade work.

defensibility.rationale: Large safety-critical software and data investment plus government projects, but US rivals had far more capital.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded US trucking autonomy firms already existed in 2019. Mars Auto stayed independent, took Korean government support (Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy projects reported 2025 and 2026) and moved to US operations.

market_need_then: US trucking autonomy attracted large 2018 and 2019 rounds (TuSimple, Plus, Embark, Kodiak) on driver shortage and freight cost; Korean logistics partner Logi Square ran trials with Mars Auto in 2020.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and ambitious: 'Superhuman AI driver', 'SHIP WITH US'

branding.brand_signature: Claim of driving without HD maps using seven cameras

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name, little brand press beyond business coverage, though Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia recognition for the CEO is reported by an unverified profile.

outcome_analysis: Mars Auto is active with about 15 staff on YC, claims more than 1.2 million autonomous miles in Korea and the US and plans unmanned trucks by 2028. It raised about $11M in March 2022 and later received Korean government support, but modest funding against US rivals means the outcome remains open.
notes: KoreaTechDesk (2022-05-03) states 15 billion won (about $11M) in March 2022 from GFT Ventures, Mirae Asset and Central, and separately names Kakao Ventures, Kakao Mobility, Y Combinator and Soma Capital as Series A investors without amount or date. Other trackers (CB Insights, a search summary) say $12M or $12.35M Series A led by GFT in March 2022; the stage label is left as other because the primary source does not label it. A one profile seed of about $1.5M is unverified. Total about $12.5M. Brand and founder facts partly rest on yespress profiles, treated as unverified. Competitor sources are from 2019. No layoff or shutdown found.
